items.title: Disrupting a coordinated model-distillation campaign
items.title_zh: 瓦解一场协同的模型蒸馏行动
items.summary: OpenAI describes how it disrupted a campaign to extract protected model reasoning and says it is strengthening defenses against adversarial distillation.

items.title: ARCagent: An Adaptive Retrieval Calibration Agent for Clinical Question Answering
items.title_zh: ARCagent：面向临床问答的自适应检索校准智能体
items.summary: ARCagent pairs a 1,706-chunk, 10-source knowledge base and a structured inter-guideline conflict registry with a conflict-aware retrieval calibration pipeline that re-ranks evidence using query-specific focus and conflict signals. On a benchmark scored by LLM-as-Judge, which the authors say avoids a 10.1-percentage-point underestimation from keyword matching, it reaches 95.3% and outperforms all base LLMs.

items.title: Breaking Babel: A Self-Evolving Multi-Agent System for Long-Form Subtitle Translation
items.title_zh: 打破巴别塔：面向长篇字幕翻译的自演化多智能体系统
items.summary: SMART is a self-evolving multi-agent system for long-form subtitle translation: a test-time training stage builds persistent episode-level memory, dynamic routing and a Mixture-of-Agents layer translate partial sentences, and a judge-refine loop updates agent prompts and routing without retraining the base LLM. The authors release the Subtitle Arena and SubMQM framework and report the best MQM score across all 15 directions, a 6.9% lower average penalty than the strongest competing agent system, and 4.50/5 in human evaluation.

items.title: Ontology-Grounded, Reasoner-Verified Benchmarks for Evaluating LLM Reasoning in Scientific AI
items.title_zh: 以本体为据、经推理器验证的科学 AI 大模型推理评测基准
items.summary: The authors propose a pipeline that automatically generates ontology-grounded multiple-choice benchmarks from any sufficiently axiomatised OWL 2 ontology, with correct answers grounded in the ontology by design and distractors whose incorrectness is formally verified by an OWL reasoner. Applied to Pizza, PMDco and DOID, it produces 112, 2,491 and 15,216 questions; six LLMs score 41.1–76.8% zero-shot, well above the 25% random baseline.

items.title: LVMH: A Meta-Optimization Harness for Long-Video Agent Memory
items.title_zh: LVMH：长视频智能体记忆的元优化框架
items.summary: LVMH is an automated multi-agent harness that frames long-video memory-policy development as multi-objective code search around a fixed answer model, separating implementation from independent review and keeping persistent meta-memory of past proposals, traces and failures. It discovers SEEM, a text-first, vision-second policy that reaches 65.7% average accuracy across three benchmarks with GPT-5, 7.7 points above the prior state of the art, at roughly 32x lower evaluation token use and 91x shorter response time.

items.title: AdaKerNet: Neural Kernel Decoding for Task-Adaptive Prediction with Multimodal Large Models
items.title_zh: AdaKerNet：面向多模态大模型任务自适应预测的神经核解码
items.summary: AdaKerNet is a task-adaptive neural kernel decoder that learns from a frozen multimodal model's representations using Lipschitz-controlled features and a reference kernel as a structural prior. Across BLIP-2, LLaVA-1.5, Qwen2.5-VL and Gemini Embedding 2 with text, audio, image and tabular inputs, it reports average error reductions of up to 41% over MLP, attention, autoencoder and kernel decoders in scarce-label regimes.

items.title: Cognitive Expert Language Models Better Align with the Corresponding Brain Systems
items.title_zh: 认知专家语言模型与对应大脑系统更契合
items.summary: The authors build expert LLM variants for six cognitive domains through prompting and fine-tuning, then test whether each expert better predicts activity in the brain system associated with that domain. Across three base models and three fMRI datasets, each expert's representations align more closely with its matching brain system, while aggregate prediction accuracy stays largely unchanged.

items.title: DeepRewind: Predicting and Repairing Premature Commitments in Deep Research Agents
items.title_zh: DeepRewind：预测并修复深度研究智能体中的过早承诺
items.summary: DeepRewind adds a control layer that represents a deep-research agent's evolving epistemic state as a typed graph of sources, evidence, claims, hypotheses, assumptions and commitments. A prompt-based world model estimates the reversibility of each intermediate conclusion, a controller blocks risky commitments and a monitor rolls back invalidated ones; across DRBench and LiveDRBench it improves insight recall by 3.6 percentage points and cuts premature commitments by 59.1% versus Open Deep Research.

items.title: GNA: Granular Neighbor Assembly for Retrieval-Augmented Multivariate Time-Series Forecasting
items.title_zh: GNA：面向检索增强多变量时间序列预测的细粒度邻居组装
items.summary: GNA is a retrieval layer for forecasting backbones that assembles neighbors at two granularities: whole past windows that keep variates coherent, and per-variate neighbors that take each variate's future from its own best-matching past. With a learned gate deciding how much to trust retrieved futures, it improves two Transformer backbones in 85 of 96 dataset-horizon settings and gives the lowest MSE on 8 of 12 standard benchmarks.

items.title: AgBench: Agentic AI Benchmarks for Personal AI Devices
items.title_zh: AgBench：面向个人 AI 设备的智能体基准
items.summary: AgBench is a benchmark and set of open artifacts for reproducibly evaluating agentic AI on personal devices across local, hybrid and cloud execution, measuring task success, latency, cloud API cost and data exposure. Based on more than 162 million data points, it finds purely local execution has lower success rates and longer completion times that worsen with concurrency, but removes cloud API cost and sensitive-data exposure; no architecture wins on every metric.

items.title: Contrastive Covariance Subspaces for Activation Steering
items.title_zh: 用于激活引导的对比协方差子空间
items.summary: Contrastive Covariance Steering is a training-free method that projects activation-steering vectors into a low-dimensional subspace obtained in closed form from a contrastive variance objective, retaining directions along which the target concept varies while suppressing directions shared with nuisance classes. Across three LLMs and four steering domains it beats all baseline steering methods in all 12 settings, with the largest relative improvements of 48–70% on AxBench and 13–27% on Emotion.

items.title: NAQD Env: A benchmark for selective withdrawal in language agents
items.title_zh: NAQD Env：语言智能体选择性撤回基准
items.summary: NAQD-Env is a synthetic benchmark that evaluates language agents' selective withdrawal — suspending affected actions, preserving unaffected work and resuming after repair — against a deterministic reference policy over explicit evidence, authorization and constraint dependencies. Across 3,150 model-prompt episodes, withdrawal recall is at most 0.06, no valid resumption is observed, and only one episode matches the full reference policy; supervised fine-tuning probes raise Qwen2.5-3B decision accuracy from 0.45–0.54 to 0.83–0.92.

items.title: SecureVibe: Making Vibe Coding More Secure
items.title_zh: SecureVibe：让氛围编程更安全
items.summary: SECUREVIBE is a training recipe that explicitly targets planning and testing for code security, combining supervised fine-tuning on four security tasks with reinforcement learning from verifiable execution feedback and hint-based self-supervision. It improves security pass@1 by 6.9 points on BaxBench and 11.5 points on SusVibes, and functionality pass@1 by 13.6 points on SusVibes and 4.1 points on SWE-bench Verified.

items.title: AnchorPrompt: Self-Distilled Soft Prompts for Robust Audio-Language Models
items.title_zh: AnchorPrompt：面向稳健音频语言模型的自蒸馏软提示
items.summary: AnchorPrompt keeps a large audio-language model frozen and learns a single block of prompt vectors inserted at the decoder input between the audio and question embeddings, trained by self-distillation over diverse audio and text perturbations. Across three models and three benchmarks it improves answer consistency, raises clean accuracy in six of nine model-benchmark pairs with at most a 1.2% impact on the rest, and reduces hallucinations under severe audio corruption while keeping false refusals on clean audio rare.

items.title: Can We Trust This Evaluation? Instance-Level Reliability of LLM-as-a-Judge
items.title_zh: 我们能信任这项评估吗？LLM 作为评判者的实例级可靠性
items.summary: SCUR is a label-free method that estimates the instance-level reliability of LLM-as-a-judge evaluations from judge-panel behavior, combining panel uncertainty, measurement cross-entropy and perturbation sensitivity into a risk score under a latent-variable measurement model. On five real benchmarks it is reported to be more effective than other methods on high-agreement risky items, a blind spot for many approaches.

items.title: Towards Robust Numerical Claim Verification
items.title_zh: 迈向稳健的数值断言验证
items.summary: The authors show that brittleness to small numerical changes persists in frontier LLMs but can be mitigated through adversarial fine-tuning on numerically perturbed examples. Parameter-efficient tuning lets small Qwen3 models (0.6B–8B) reach 98.7% accuracy on label-flipping perturbations, above GPT-5.4 Pro (74.0%) and Gemini 2.5 Flash (73.9%), and the gains generalise to unseen perturbation types and cross-lingual transfer.

items.title: ATLAS: Aligned Transport of Latent Structure for Reliable World Model Planning
items.title_zh: ATLAS：面向可靠世界模型规划的对齐潜在结构传输
items.summary: ATLAS is a training objective that preserves relational geometry from an informative encoder representation in the latent used for world-model planning, while calibrating its marginal distribution through Wasserstein embedding matching. Instantiated in LeWM, it improves goal-reaching success on PushT, TwoRoom and OGBench-Cube, with the largest gain on higher-novelty TwoRoom episodes.

items.title: Better Nearest Neighbor Graph Indices via (Efficient) LLM-Guided Pruning
items.title_zh: 借助（高效）LLM 引导剪枝改进最近邻图索引
items.summary: LGP uses LLM reasoning to refine an existing approximate nearest neighbor graph index, replacing structurally low-value neighbors with LLM-selected alternatives while retaining the graph's sparsity and navigability. Experiments on semantic retrieval benchmarks show consistent end-to-end gains over both greedy graph search and LLM-based reranking on indices such as DiskANN and HNSW.

items.title: Engineering Simplicity: Simple Mechanism Interfaces Steer LLM Agents
items.title_zh: 工程化的简洁：简单的机制接口引导 LLM 智能体
items.summary: Across auctions and matching tasks, the authors compare interfaces that elicit a complete bid or ranking with sequential interfaces and vary reasoning scaffolds across four model families. The ascending auction interface substantially reduces bid deviations and explaining why truth-telling is safe improves choices, while prompts to plan through matching rounds or form beliefs about opponents worsen play; these behavioral gains do not appear in the agents' stated plans.

items.title: In-Context Learning Amplifies a Latent Symbolic Circuit
items.title_zh: 上下文学习会放大潜在的符号电路
items.summary: Tracing a three-stage abstraction, induction and retrieval circuit across shot counts in three model families, the author finds the circuit is detectable and functional well before models achieve high accuracy. Per-head causal contribution grows up to 8x from 1-shot to 10-shot, and cross-shot activation patching raises accuracy from 1% to 56% at 0-shot and from 17% to 88% at 1-shot.

items.title: Benchmarking System One decision models against trained classifiers and language models for automated decision gates
items.title_zh: System One 决策模型、分类器与语言模型在自动决策门禁上的基准比较
items.summary: The authors send the same semantic requests to eight typed decision-model checkpoints, the hosted model Jev and four open generative models, and score trained and zero-shot classifiers on the same workflow, intent, emotion and social-science items. With labels, a fine-tuned DeBERTa-v3-large is the most accurate on every benchmark but one; without labels no decision model is significantly more accurate than Jev on workflows or intents, and the paper documents calibration and label-order sensitivity issues that shape design rules for automated decision gates.

items.title: Re-ranking and Late Interaction Drive Retrieval Quality: A Controlled Comparison of RAG Strategies for Scientific Question Answering
items.title_zh: 重排序与后期交互驱动检索质量：科学问答中 RAG 策略的受控比较
items.summary: The authors compare six retrieval strategies for scientific question answering — dense top-k retrieval, LLM query rephrasing, rephrasing plus LLM reranking, reciprocal rank fusion, agentic tool-call retrieval and ColBERTv2 late interaction — over 463,971 arXiv papers with a shared Llama-3.1-8B generator and evaluation protocol. They release the code and a synthetic dataset of 19,484 questions and assess answer quality and gold-paper retrieval with an LLM judge.

items.title: Vision-Language-Action Autonomous Driving Agent with Language-based Memory
items.title_zh: 具备语言记忆的视觉-语言-动作自动驾驶智能体
items.summary: AD-Memo is a general vision-language-action driving agent that outputs memories of key surrounding objects as an extension of its chain of thought and makes that memory part of subsequent input. Trained in two stages with supervised fine-tuning and a semi-closed-loop reinforcement learning algorithm called Da Capo, it improves driving quality and driving-scene question answering at all-way-stop intersections and in general driving, and produces memory that other models can plug in.

items.title: Legal Research Bench: Measuring End-to-End Reliability in Long-Horizon Legal Research Agents
items.title_zh: 法律研究基准：衡量长时程法律研究智能体的端到端可靠性
items.summary: Legal Research Bench is a set of 413 expert-written U.S. legal research questions, each paired with a gold answer, supporting authorities and a binary rubric, scored all-pass with source verification. Evaluating thirteen frontier models in a harness with web search, case-law search, page parsing and retrieval tools, the strongest, Claude Opus 4.8, is fully correct on 42.9% of questions, and more turns, tool calls and inference cost do not predict higher accuracy.

items.title: PLDiv: Measuring Dataset Diversity and Semantic Collapse via Persistence Landscapes
items.title_zh: PLDiv：通过持久景观衡量数据集多样性与语义坍缩
items.summary: PLDiv is a diversity metric derived from persistence landscapes that summarizes how data neighborhoods evolve as nearby samples progressively connect, giving an interpretable scalar for structural diversity without task-specific supervision. It performs competitively on text generations and image embeddings and detects semantic collapse in instruction datasets and reasoning trajectories, supporting synthetic-data monitoring, dataset construction and augmentation.

items.title_zh: OpenAI DevDay 2026 回顾
items.summary: OpenAI's DevDay 2026 recap collects more than 20 announcements spanning GPT-6 Astra, ChatGPT, Codex, APIs, security and new tools for builders.

items.title: ByteDance’s Doubao reportedly preparing personal AI agent, codenamed Spell and tested since April
items.title_zh: 字节跳动豆包据悉筹备代号 Spell 的个人 AI 智能体
items.summary: ByteDance's Doubao is reportedly accelerating work on a new personal AI agent codenamed Spell, which sources say has been in internal testing.

items.title: Can large language models unlock discrete data in ophthalmic diagnostic reports?
items.title_zh: 大语言模型能否解锁眼科诊断报告中的离散数据？
items.summary: A small proof-of-concept study ran two GPT-4o-assisted pipelines over 20 de-identified ophthalmic diagnostic PDF reports to extract structured data against a reconciled manual ground truth. Prompt-only extraction reached 100% value accuracy across all four report types, schema-constrained output reached 100% formatting accuracy, and mean extraction time fell from 56.51 seconds per report manually to about 5 seconds.
